Synopsis:
    The Trump administration has struck an unprecedented deal giving private firm NABEP — controlled by Venezuelan businessman Alejandro Betancourt — 100-year leases over 17 Venezuelan oilfields (~65bn barrels). The US takes a 35% equity stake and 20% guaranteed production offtake. The deal is generating friction: major US oil companies (ExxonMobil, ConocoPhillips) remain hesitant due to legal uncertainty and concerns about competing with the US government itself in Venezuela. Separately, Chevron, Eni, Shell, BP and others are progressing on distinct contract migrations and offshore gas licenses under Venezuela's energy reform. The NABEP structure raises governance and compliance red flags due to Betancourt's background, complicating Trump's goal of rapidly scaling Venezuelan oil output.
